LESSON: TOPOGRAPHICAL MAPS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Natural and Historic Built Environments
Topic 4.1: Topographical maps
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Topographical maps, part of Natural and Historic Built Environments in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9 SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: howing human activities, display the cross-sections and take a gallery walk and peer assessment. Why are topographic maps important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. sign terms and concepts related to the topographical map,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Topographical maps in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. describe human activities on topographical maps,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Topographical maps in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. use creative and critical thinking skills to enlarge and reduce parts of topographical maps,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Topographical maps in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. illustrate cross-sections from topographical maps,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Topographical maps in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. appreciate representation of human activities on topographical maps. ●

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Topographical maps in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. sign terms and concepts related to the topographical map,

   Topographical maps helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. describe human activities on topographical maps,

   Topographical maps helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. use creative and critical thinking skills to enlarge and reduce parts of topographical maps,

   Topographical maps helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. illustrate cross-sections from topographical maps,

   Topographical maps helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. appreciate representation of human activities on topographical maps. ●

   Topographical maps helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Topographical maps together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Digital literacy: learners enhance their digital technology skills as they use digital devices to find out how human activities are

represented in topographical maps.

● Learning to Learn: learners develop relationships as they brainstorm in groups on human activities that may be represented in a

topographical map and share what they have learnt with peers.

Values:
• Unity: learners take turns in conversations as they brainstorm on human activities that may be represented in a topographical map.

• Integrity: learners exhibit transparency and fairness as they display the cross-sections and take a gallery walk and peer assessment.

12

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Self Esteem: as learners draw and display cross-sections from topographical maps showing human activities in class for peer

assessment.

● Peer teaching: as learners display the cross-sections and take a gallery walk and peer assess.

Link to other learning areas:

Creative arts and Mathematics: as the earner draws a sketch map to enlarge and reduce part of a topographical maps and present to peers.

Suggested learning Resources;

approved textbooks and other printed resources, photographs, pictures, vetted digital devices, internet sources ,display boards,

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. sign terms and concepts related to the topographical map,
2. describe human activities on topographical maps,
3. use creative and critical thinking skills to enlarge and reduce parts of topographical maps,
4. illustrate cross-sections from topographical maps,
5. appreciate representation of human activities on topographical maps. ●
